name: Surface-based Instancing with Noise Modulation
definition: A technique where surface primitives are represented by instanced points (roughly 400 million per primitive) to achieve smooth results at 1024x1024 pixels, using a frustum-shaped voxel buffer of resolution ~1200x1200x250. Density is modulated by noise, which requires instantiating a point and evaluating the full fractal noise function before culling if density is zero.
summary: Surface-based Instancing with Noise Modulation renders volumetric primitives by distributing instanced points on a parametric surface, using procedural noise to modulate density and displacement rather than learned parameters.
